Which Southampton, NY office sends the tax bill?

The Town of Southampton Receiver of Taxes bills and collects from December 1 through May 31, and the Suffolk County Comptroller takes over after that. The Receiver's office sits on the main floor of Town Hall at 116 Hampton Road, phone 631-702-2470, with weekday counter hours of 8:30 a.m. through 4:00 p.m. The Assessor, who sets the value your bill is built on, works from the same address and answers at 631-283-6020.

Southampton is a large town on the South Fork of Long Island. The Census Bureau lists 293.5 square miles, but only 139.1 of those are land, because the Atlantic Ocean and Peconic Bay take the rest. Inside the town are seven incorporated villages (North Haven, Quogue, Sag Harbor, Sagaponack, Southampton, Westhampton Beach and West Hampton Dunes) and 16 hamlets, among them Hampton Bays, Bridgehampton, Flanders and Shinnecock Hills. If you are unsure which bill covers your address, call the Receiver before you sign a contract.

  • Receiver of Taxes: bills, receipts, duplicate bills, address changes, first-half and second-half payments.
  • Assessor: values, exemption applications, grievance forms, the tentative roll.
  • County Comptroller: every unpaid balance after May 31, plus tax liens.

When are Southampton property taxes due for the 2026-27 bill?

First-half payment is owed by January 10, 2027, and because that is a Sunday the Town moves the deadline to Monday, January 11. Second-half payment is owed by May 31, 2027. Bills go out by December 15, but the Receiver cannot mail them or take money until the Suffolk County Legislature approves the tax warrant, which usually comes after the lien date of December 1, 2026.

Not receiving a bill does not extend the penalty-free period. New York law holds the owner responsible either way, and the Town's online portal can print a duplicate bill. Mailed payments count by the USPS postmark on the envelope. A private metered postmark does not count, so send certified mail if you are near a deadline.

What does late payment cost in Southampton?

First-half tax paid after January 10 still goes to the Receiver, with 1 percent interest added to the base amount for each month. Anything unpaid after May 31 draws a 5 percent penalty and 5 percent interest, and the Town cannot accept those payments. They go to the County Comptroller, who adds a further 1 percent a month until the balance is cleared.

Partial payments are possible. The Receiver takes installments of at least $200 under Suffolk County Resolution 551-2001, and interest then runs only on the unpaid balance. The Comptroller also accepts partial payments on delinquent tax. The county phone for balance questions is 631-852-3000, and the Comptroller's mailing address is 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901.

  • Online: $1.75 for an ACH payment, or a 2.5 percent fee by credit card, charged by the processor and not by the Town.
  • By mail: check payable to Receiver of Taxes, drawn on a U.S. bank, or a money order.
  • A check or ACH payment returned by your bank for any reason cancels the tax payment.

How do I look up my Southampton tax bill and change the mailing address?

Use the Town's eTax portal, where the easiest search is by street address. You can also search by owner last name, tax map number or the current bill number, and no username or password is required. The record shows the owner, tax map number, zoning and taxes due. For help with the portal, the Citizens' Response Center answers at 631-702-2440 on weekdays, 8:30 a.m. onward until the 4 p.m. close.

A missing bill usually means the Town has an old mailing address. Send a change-of-address form to 116 Hampton Road, Southampton, NY 11968, fax it to 631-287-5732 or drop a copy at Town Hall. The portal's Duplicate Tax Bill option prints a fresh copy at once. Suffolk County also advises owners to tell the Assessor about any new mailing address so the roll is corrected before bills go out in December.

Before you list, pull the bill for the current year and confirm the Property Location box in the upper left corner. It carries the official street address and house number. Chapter 239 of the Southampton Town Code requires house numbers to be clearly visible from the street, a rule the Town ties to emergency response.

How do I challenge a Southampton assessment or claim an exemption?

File a grievance by Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. The Assessor's Office at Town Hall helps with the application the week before, and appointments go through 631-283-6020. The Town's tentative roll appears around May 1, so review it first. The town review board decides complaints, and it meets again off and on from June through September to work through filings.

The Town's own grievance page gives the state equalization rate and residential assessment ratio for Southampton as 59.7 percent. Keep that ratio in mind when you set your assessed value beside a sale price or appraisal.

Exemptions need an application at the Assessor by March 1. The Town lists these programs:

  • STAR and Enhanced STAR for primary residences.
  • Senior citizens.
  • Veterans.
  • Persons with disabilities and limited incomes.
  • First-time homebuyers.
  • Volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers.

Suffolk County warns that a buyer does not inherit a seller's veterans or senior exemption, so the bill can rise sharply after a sale.

What happens to unpaid Southampton tax when I sell the house?

Unpaid tax stays attached to the property, so it has to be settled at or before closing. Your closing attorney or title company will request a tax payoff from the Receiver before May 31, or from the County Comptroller after it. Send them the full tax-bill description of the parcel, since the Comptroller asks for it on every inquiry.

Suffolk's collection path is slower than many people expect. After May 31 the County sells a tax lien to itself, usually in the autumn or December. A one-, two- or three-family home can be redeemed within 36 months of the lien sale, other property within 12, and after that the County issues a tax deed. The Town's FAQ says the Treasurer typically starts collection on vacant land after one year and on improved property after three years of non-payment. Redemption after a deed is handled by the Suffolk Department of Planning, Division of Real Estate, at 631-853-5900.

If you paid off a mortgage during the tax year, check with the Receiver whether the bank already paid the full year. The Town notes that the bank will not necessarily forward that information, and the owner stays liable for late-payment penalties.

What do Southampton's numbers and climate mean for a seller?

Southampton homes carry high values, and the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 figures show it: homes valued at a $928,100 median, 82.4 percent of them lived in by owners, and a median household income of $128,594. Median gross rent is $2,363. The 2025 population estimate is 71,601, up from 69,036 in the 2020 census.

Weather tends to show up at inspection. NOAA normals cited by Wikipedia put Bridgehampton at about 49.8 inches of yearly precipitation and 26.8 inches of snow, and the town sits at about 26 feet above sea level on average. Buyers of waterfront and low-lying properties often ask about drainage and flood history, so gather those records before listing. The Long Island Rail Road's Montauk Branch stops in Speonk, Westhampton, Hampton Bays, Southampton and Bridgehampton.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Southampton property tax in person?

At the Receiver of Taxes on the main floor of Town Hall, 116 Hampton Road, weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Cash, checks and money orders are accepted, and you can also pay online or by mail.

Can I pay Southampton property tax in two parts?

Yes. One half is owed by January 10 (January 11 in 2027) and the other half by May 31. Smaller partial payments of at least $200 are also accepted, with interest charged only on the remaining balance.

What happens if I miss the May 31 deadline in Southampton?

Payment moves to the Suffolk County Comptroller, and the balance picks up a 5 percent penalty plus interest. The Town can no longer take your payment after that date.

When is the Southampton exemption deadline?

March 1 for new or renewed exemptions, filed with the Assessor at 116 Hampton Road. Call 631-283-6020 to ask which application fits your situation.

Do I still owe tax if my Southampton bill never arrived?

Yes. Under New York law the owner is responsible for the tax whether or not a bill arrives. Ask the Receiver for a duplicate or print one from the Town's tax portal.

Who bills and collects property tax in Syracuse, NY?

The City Payment Center prepares the bill and takes payment for City, School and County property tax together, while the Department of Assessment sets the value. Both are in City Hall at 233 East Washington Street. The Payment Center is in Room 122, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and its phone is 315-448-8310. Assessment is in Suite 130 at 315-448-8270.

The Payment Center services more than 42,000 taxpayer accounts. It also enforces collection of delinquent property tax and handles the sale of tax-delinquent properties. Enter City Hall from the Market Street side, expect a security check, and know that on-street parking nearby is metered.

Syracuse is the Onondaga County seat. The Census Bureau counts 25.06 square miles of land, which works out to about 5,930 residents per square mile in 2020.

  • Payment Center: bills, payments, delinquent tax, tax trust payment plans.
  • Assessment: values, exemptions, change of address for notices, grievance forms.
  • Onondaga County Clerk: copies of deeds.

When are Syracuse property taxes due?

Ask the City Payment Center at 315-448-8310 for the due dates on your current bill. The same office can tell you what you owe today and whether any prior year is open. A tax question that lands at the Assessment office is routed to the Payment Center, which oversees taxes.

If the bill has gone to the wrong place, file a Change of Address for City Service Notifications with the Department of Assessment. That form covers tax bills, assessment notices and other property notices, so owners who have moved or inherited a house should file it before the next bill cycle.

Homeowners who have fallen behind can apply for a tax trust, which is the City's payment plan for delinquent property tax. The application is a PDF on the Payment Center page. Parcels that go through tax foreclosure are transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, known as the Land Bank, and are then offered for sale there.

How do I challenge my Syracuse assessment?

File a formal grievance with the Board of Assessment Review during the last two weeks of January. The board is made up of four or five officers appointed by the City Council, and it can reduce an assessment for good cause. Grounds include an assessment that is unequal, excessive or unlawful, and a wrong property classification.

Fill out the grievance form, print it and sign it by hand. Bring or mail it to City Hall, Suite 130. The office accepts only forms with an original signature, complete documentation, and a filing date inside those two weeks. Forms that arrive early or late are not taken. The office has posted evening and Saturday-morning hours during the window.

New York State law requires assessors to hold every property at a uniform percentage of market value (RPTL sections 301 and 305). Syracuse assesses by cost, income and comparable sales, then adjusts for physical changes or market shifts. Each parcel has its own market value, which is why neighbors' assessments differ.

Why did my Syracuse tax bill go up, and who can explain a charge?

A bill rises when the assessment changes, an exemption status changes, the tax rate moves, or a special charge not tied to assessment is added or increased. That is the Department of Assessment's own list. If a charge on your bill is unfamiliar, call 315-448-8270 and staff will look into it.

Physical changes matter too. Building or tearing down a porch or garage can change an assessment to match the new value. Properties are valued by accepted real estate methods, which can include cost, income and comparable sales, with adjustments for physical changes or the market.

To find out who owns a parcel, the Department points to the SDG Image Mate lookup by address. It does not keep owner phone numbers. The City also maintains tax maps that show lot dimensions but not buildings, so a boundary question needs a private survey from the seller's files.

Which Syracuse tax exemptions can I claim, and by when?

A property cannot take both the senior and the disability exemption on one account. Renewal forms for the income-based programs are mailed each August and must be back before January 1. The Department also lists a historic property exemption and property improvement exemptions for renovating vacant, residential and commercial buildings.

Get a written payoff from the City Payment Center and ask whether the County and School portions are included. The Payment Center collects all three, so one figure should cover them. Then confirm with your closing attorney that any tax trust balance is paid off at the closing table.

  • Get a copy of your deed from the Onondaga County Clerk, which keeps the official deed records.
  • Check the City's tax map of your parcel. It shows lot lines but not buildings, so a seller usually supplies a private survey.
  • If the exemption on your bill is a senior or disability exemption, tell the buyer it will not carry over.

Syracuse averages about 115.6 inches of snow a year, so ask your inspector to look closely at the roof, gutters and drainage before you list.

What do Syracuse housing numbers look like?

Syracuse is a city of renters. Census QuickFacts for 2020-2024 give an owner-occupancy rate of 41.6 percent, a median owner-occupied value of $138,400 and a median gross rent of $1,039. Median household income is $47,819. The 2020 census counted 148,620 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 144,896.

The Syracuse City School District covers the whole city and runs 34 schools plus four alternative programs. The city recognizes 26 neighborhoods, from University Hill and Tipperary Hill to the north and south sides, and it sits at the crossing of I-81 and I-90. Syracuse University and SUNY Upstate Medical University anchor the economy, and Micron began building a large chip complex in the northern suburbs in 2024.

At the City Payment Center, Room 122 in City Hall, 233 East Washington Street, Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. It collects City, School and County tax in one place.

When is Syracuse Grievance filing season?

The last two weeks of January each year. The forms must be signed in ink and delivered to City Hall, Suite 130, inside that window.

Can I get a payment plan for back taxes in Syracuse?

Yes. The City Payment Center offers a tax trust for homeowners who have fallen behind. Pick up the application from the Payment Center page or call 315-448-8310.

Does the STAR credit lower a Syracuse bill directly?

Only for owners registered before 2015. Newer registrants get a credit check or direct deposit from New York State, which they use to pay City and School tax.

What happens to a Syracuse house after tax foreclosure?

It is transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, the Land Bank, which lists available properties for sale.

Which Tonawanda does this guide cover, and who collects the tax?

This guide covers the Town of Tonawanda in Erie County, the northern inner-ring suburb of Buffalo, and not the separate City of Tonawanda to its north. The Town Assessor's Office, reachable at 716-877-8811, sets values and runs exemptions and grievances. Tax payments are handled through the Town Clerk's office and an online payment portal.

The town was established in 1836 and includes the Village of Kenmore, which together are often called Ken-Ton. It covers 18.7 square miles of land, with the Niagara River on the west, the Erie Canal along Tonawanda Creek on the north and Niagara Falls Boulevard (US 62) on the east. A Kenmore address can carry a village tax on top of the town and county bills, so check your bill for a village line.

  • Town of Tonawanda Assessor: values, STAR questions, exemptions, grievance applications.
  • Town Clerk's Office: in-person partial payments on weekdays.
  • Erie County Clerk, 25 Delaware Avenue, Buffalo: small claims assessment petitions.

When are Tonawanda property taxes due?

The Town publishes three separate bills with their own due dates. For the 2025/26 cycle the county and town bill was due February 15 with a last payment date of June 30, the school bill October 16 with a last payment date of November 30, and the village bill July 3 with a last payment date of November 1. Check your own bill for the dates that apply to the next cycle.

The Town lists two school districts, Ken-Ton and Sweet Home, because part of the town lies in each.

What penalties apply to late Tonawanda tax?

County and town tax grows by a step each fortnight after the due date: 1.5 percent from February 19 to March 2, 3 percent from March 3 to 16, 4.5 percent from March 17 to 31, 6 percent from April 1 to 15 and 7.5 percent from April 16 to 30. School tax carries 7.5 percent for October 15 to 31 and 9 percent for November. Village tax carries 7.5 percent for July and another 1.5 percent for each month after.

Online payment is available for tax bills, and the convenience fee depends on the method. A credit card costs 2.45 percent, a Visa debit card is a flat $3.95, other bank debit cards cost 1.50 percent and an electronic check is a flat $1.75. Electronic checks take about two weeks to process, so do not use one close to a deadline. The Town does not keep those fees, since the web service provider collects them.

Partial tax payments cannot be made online. They are taken in person only, by cash, check or charge card, at the Town Clerk's Office, open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:00 in the afternoon.

What are the 2025 Tonawanda tax rates?

The Town's rate page gives these 2025 homestead totals: 35.481651 for county and town tax outside the village and 24.476354 inside the village. The county line alone is 15.404260, and the Town of Tonawanda line is 20.077391. These are the figures for owner-occupied residential property, which the Town calls homestead.

  • School tax for 2025/2026: Ken-Ton 59.1567004 and Sweet Home 45.787477 for homestead property.
  • Village homestead tax: 40.342600 for 2025.
  • Equalization rate: the Town reports a 21 percent level of assessment for 2025.

That 21 percent ratio means assessed values run well below market. A house with a full-market value near $200,000 would be carried at an assessed value of about $42,000. Compare your own assessment to the ratio before you decide a grievance is warranted.

Which exemptions and relief programs apply in the Town of Tonawanda?

The Town and the Village of Kenmore offer exemptions for limited-income seniors, veterans, disabled persons with limited incomes, volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers, nonprofits and clergy, plus business investment exemptions under RPTL 485-a and 485-b. New York State administers Basic and Enhanced STAR directly, so the Assessor's Office no longer takes STAR applications. Every owner-occupied house is eligible for STAR.

Veterans can choose one of two exemptions. The alternative veterans exemption (RPTL 458-a) covers wartime service or an expeditionary medal, and the Cold War exemption (RPTL 458-b) covers service in that period. Either one applies only to county, city, town and village taxes and not to school district or special district taxes. Veterans must file the first application by March 1, because the exemption is not automatic.

For lost tax returns or proof of income, the Assessor's Office can advise on the non-filer worksheets the Town provides for seniors and disabled applicants. Call 716-877-8811 with questions about which form fits you.

How do I challenge a Tonawanda assessment?

Start with an informal review between February 1 and April 1, then file a formal application for the Board of Assessment Review, which hears complaints on Grievance Day, May 25 in 2027. Applications are available at the Assessor's Office from May 1. To schedule a hearing, call 716-877-8811 after May 2, or file for a non-hearing review by 9 p.m. on Grievance Day.

Residential challenges use form RP 524 plus the Board's residential information sheet with comparable sales in section 2. If the Board does not satisfy you, a Small Claims Assessment Review petition costs $30 and must be filed by July 30 with the Erie County Clerk. You qualify only if you own and live in a one-, two- or three-family home, filed a timely complaint with the Board and ask for no bigger reduction than you sought there. Prepare at least eight copies.

The taxable status date is March 1, and exemption applications are due the same day. Veterans exemptions are not automatic. The Town administers senior, veterans, disability and firefighter exemptions, and New York State runs STAR directly.

What does a Tonawanda seller need before closing?

Call the Building Department at 716-877-8801 for a certificate of compliance for the storm water system, because the Town says you need one to sell your property. The inspection generally covers the sump pump and its electric line, footing drains, yard drains and downspouts. Book it early so a failed item does not delay closing.

Permit records for the house are available from the Building Department only from 1965 on, since earlier plans were destroyed. The Town's deferred-payment loan programs also matter at sale. Under the Residential Rehabilitation loan, the balance becomes due when the house is sold or the deed changes, and the loan is secured by a mortgage filed with the Erie County Clerk. First-time homebuyer loans have the same trigger.

Census QuickFacts for 2020-2024 give Tonawanda town an owner-occupancy rate of 72.2 percent, a median owner-occupied value of $213,900, median gross rent of $1,098 and median household income of $77,673. Is Tonawanda town the same as Tonawanda city?

No. The Town of Tonawanda is a separate municipality in Erie County, and the City of Tonawanda lies to its north. Check which one appears on your tax bill.

Can I pay part of my Tonawanda tax bill online?

No. Partial payments are only taken in person at the Town Clerk's Office on weekdays, with a 4:00 p.m. close.

When is Grievance Day in the Town of Tonawanda?

Tuesday, May 25, 2027, the fourth Tuesday of the month. Applications are available at the Assessor's Office from May 1.

How much does a Tonawanda small claims assessment petition cost?

The filing fee is $30, and it may be refunded if you prevail. The petition goes to the Erie County Clerk by July 30.

Must I schedule an inspection before selling in the Town of Tonawanda?

Yes, a certificate of compliance for the storm water system. Call the Building Department at 716-877-8801 to schedule it.

Who bills property tax in White Plains, NY?

The City of White Plains Finance Department bills and collects it at City Hall, 255 Main Street, Room 102, and the City Assessor sets the values it is based on. White Plains is a city of about ten square miles and the seat of Westchester County, so one household can receive a city and school bill in July and January, and a county bill in April.

Bills are made out to the owner of record. Under RPTL 922, a bill that never reaches the owner does not cancel the tax or stop penalties and interest from running. If one fails to arrive, the Finance Department asks owners to call 914-422-1248 so the address can be verified and a duplicate mailed.

  • Finance Department: payments, bill copies, address changes and payoff figures. The city lists 914-422-1235 for tax office questions.
  • Assessor, 255 Main Street, phone 914-422-1223: assessed value, exemptions, parcel information and complaint forms.
  • Board of Assessment Review: hears complaints that an assessment is unequal, excessive or misclassified.

When are White Plains property taxes due?

Taxes come due three times a year: July 1 and January 1 for city and school tax, and April 1 for county tax. The city allows payment through the last day of each month without interest, so the practical deadlines are July 31, January 31 and April 30.

Due dateLate afterWhat it covers

The city's FAQ says bills are mailed in mid-December, late March and June. Payments must be postmarked or hand-delivered by the due date, or they carry interest. Overdue tax and water charges accrue interest at 1 percent a month, and the city states that state law gives it no power to waive that interest for any reason.

How do I pay a White Plains tax bill?

You can pay in person, online, by mail or by automatic debit. City Hall accepts payments from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on days other than holidays, at the Finance Department window in Room 102.

  • Mail with the stub: make the check out to the Commissioner of Finance and send it to P.O. Box 5086, White Plains, NY 10602-5086.
  • Mail without the stub: send the check to the Finance Department at 255 Main Street, Room 102, and write your section, block and lot number on it.
  • Online: the city runs an online portal for tax and water payments by credit card.
  • Direct payment: sign an authorization agreement and the city debits a checking or savings account when each installment is due.

Ownership changes are recorded by the Assessor, who needs a certified copy of the recorded deed. A change of mailing address for billing goes in on the Tax Account Change Form. Owners can also name a consenting third party to receive copies of bills, using the Third Party Notification Form.

How do I challenge a White Plains assessment?

File a complaint on form RP-524 between January 1 and January 21 with the Assessor or the Board of Assessment Review. The Board meets on January 21 under the City Charter, and on Thursday, January 21, 2027 it sits by appointment from 3 to 5 p.m. and 7 to 9 p.m. in the Common Council Chambers, Room 203, at City Hall. Call 914-422-1223 to book a time.

White Plains runs on a different calendar from towns that hold a May grievance day. The Assessor's page gives the schedule as follows: taxable status date December 1, tentative roll January 1, final roll March 1, and exemptions processed from April 1 through December 1. A late complaint loses the right to review, so mark January on the calendar before you list.

Bring evidence of market value, such as recent sales of comparable homes nearby or an appraisal. The Board decides whether an assessment is unequal, excessive or in the wrong class.

How is a White Plains tax bill figured?

Two things set it: the property's taxable assessment and the levies of the jurisdictions that tax it. The Finance Department explains that the tax rate is the levy divided by the total taxable assessed value, and the assessment reflects the property's value less any exemptions the owner qualifies for.

That is why an exemption can change a bill without touching the city's budget. The Assessor processes exemption applications from April 1 through December 1 each year, and the Assessor's page says various property tax exemptions may be available through that office. Ask the Assessor which exemptions are on your parcel before you give a buyer a bill to rely on.

Why do water charges matter when selling in White Plains?

Unpaid water charges do not disappear. The Finance Department's FAQ says they are relevied against the property as a tax lien on the following July 1. A seller with an old water balance can therefore find it folded into the next tax bill and into the payoff.

Residential water in the city is divided into six districts, each billed twice a year, and a final water reading costs $75 when requested by calling 914-422-1211. Schedule the reading with the closing so the water account closes cleanly and the buyer starts with a clear record. If the property has water service, an available-on-demand charge based on meter size is billed even when no water is used.

What do Census figures say about White Plains homes?

The Census Bureau counts 62,871 White Plains residents in July 2025, up 5.6 percent from the April 2020 base. Owners hold 51.0 percent of homes, so renters are nearly half of households, and the 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $620,800.

Median monthly owner costs run $3,525 with a mortgage and $1,494 without one, and median gross rent is $2,269. The city has 25,578 households averaging 2.31 people, and the median household income is $110,763. White Plains covers only 9.74 square miles of land, which works out to 6,116.8 people per square mile.

The city grew up as a retail and office hub. It became a village in 1866 and a city in 1916, and its downtown was rebuilt around the Westchester County Courthouse and the Galleria in the 1970s. The city government puts the weekday daytime population near 250,000.

What should I check before selling a White Plains house with tax due?

Ask the Finance Department for a payoff that includes city, school, county and any water relevy, and confirm the date to which interest is calculated. A few steps keep the sale clean.

  • Check which of the July, January and April installments are paid.
  • Ask whether any water charges were relevied on a July 1 bill.
  • Make sure the Assessor has the current deed and owner name on file.
  • If you plan to contest the value, file by January 21, since a late complaint loses the right to review.

A cash buyer can close with open tax, and the title company pays the balance from the proceeds. Since interest is 1 percent each month, a closing date that slips past month end changes the number.

Frequently asked questions

When are White Plains property taxes due?

City and school tax is due July 1 and January 1, and county tax is due April 1. The city accepts payment through the last day of each of those months, and interest applies after that.

What is the White Plains late interest rate?

It is 1 percent a month on overdue taxes and water charges. The Finance Department says state law prevents it from waiving interest or penalties on a late payment.

When is White Plains grievance day?

There is no May grievance day. Complaints are filed January 1 through January 21 with the Assessor or the Board of Assessment Review, which meets on January 21 by appointment. Call 914-422-1223.

Can I set up automatic payments for White Plains taxes?

Yes. Sign and return the city's authorization agreement to the Finance Department at 255 Main Street, Room 102. The city then debits your checking or savings account on each due date.

How do I change the owner name on a White Plains tax bill?

Only the Assessor's Office can record a change of ownership, and it needs a certified copy of the recorded deed. A change of mailing address goes through the Tax Account Change Form.

How many property tax bills does a Yonkers homeowner get?

Two a year. The City of Yonkers sends one in March for Westchester County tax and one in July for city and school tax. The city's tax page says the county bill is paid once, usually in April, and the city and school bill is split into three equal installments with three stubs at the bottom.

Yonkers is the largest city in Westchester County, with 212,603 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, and the Tax Office sits in City Hall at 40 South Broadway. The Assessment Department in the same building sets the values that the bills are built on. The city offers an online property tax portal where any parcel can be researched for free.

  • Tax Office, City Hall Room 108: payments, bill copies and payment history. The owner can call 914-377-6138, 914-377-6141 or 914-377-6146.
  • Assessment Department, City Hall, phone 914-377-6200: parcel updates, exemptions and assessment appeals.
  • Cashier's Office, first floor of City Hall, Room 108: in-person payments.

When are Yonkers property taxes due?

For the 2026 and 2027 city and school bill, installments fall on July 24, 2026, October 6, 2026 and January 6, 2027. The first date moves each year because it is set 30 days after the City Council adopts the budget, usually in June. The second is always October 6 and the third is always January 6, shifted off a weekend.

The county bill is adopted around March and falls due 30 days later, so the 2027 date will depend on when the county passes its budget. As of mid-November 2026, the third city installment is the next one on the calendar.

What happens if I pay a Yonkers tax installment late?

Interest starts immediately, because the Tax Office allows no grace period on an installment. The rate is 15 percent a year, simple interest, calculated daily from the confirmation date through the day of payment. The city says it cannot waive that interest for any reason.

The office decides whether a payment arrived on time by the postmark on the envelope. Local banks no longer accept Yonkers tax payments, so mail goes to City of Yonkers, 40 South Broadway, Room 108, Yonkers, NY 10701. Online payment by credit card or electronic check is also available, and the Yonkers site points owners to Yonkers.MunicipalTaxPayments.com to see outstanding taxes.

If you receive a delinquent notice for a bill you already paid, mail a copy of the front and back of the check and any receipt to the Tax Office at City Hall. Owners who get a delinquent tax letter are told to review the parcel in the online portal for details.

How do I challenge a Yonkers assessment?

File a complaint with the Board of Assessment Review between November 1 and November 15. Yonkers uses a fall calendar rather than a May grievance day. The Assessment Department's calendar sets a July 1 valuation date, an October 15 taxable status date and a November 1 tentative roll.

  • November 1 to 15: grievance period for complaints to the Board.
  • December 15: deadline to send additional information or ask for a personal hearing.
  • Last Monday in January through the third Friday in February: personal hearings.
  • April 10 to May 10: window to file Small Claims Assessment Review or certiorari, open only to owners who already filed a protest with the Board.

The final roll is published on April 10. If this year's window has already closed when you read this, the next one opens November 1, 2027, and an owner who plans to sell can mention a pending protest to the buyer.

When must Yonkers exemption applications be filed?

By October 15 each year. That is the deadline for senior citizen, disability and veteran exemption filings and renewals, and it moves to the next business day when it lands on a weekend or holiday. The Assessment Department asks owners to apply by September 15 if they can.

The exemption stays on the roll only if it is renewed, so a seller who has had one for years should confirm the renewal is current. Ask the Assessment Department at 914-377-6200 what is on file for your parcel.

What do title companies need from the Yonkers Tax Office?

They can research a parcel online for free, or they can pay a $5 fee per property per year for the Tax Department to research it. Title and mortgage companies are encouraged to use the city's online property portal and the municipal tax payment site first. Without a processed fee the office gives no information by phone or email, and it asks for two to three weeks of lead time.

Make checks for that fee payable to the City of Yonkers at 40 South Broadway, Room 108. If you are the seller, order the payoff early. Owners can also ask the Tax Office for copies of prior or current bills and for a history of payments.

What do Census figures say about Yonkers homes?

Yonkers has 81,645 households with an average of 2.53 people. Only 46.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so renters hold a majority, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $501,600 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $1,784.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $3,028, compared with $1,356 for owners without one. The median household income is $83,549, and 13.8 percent of residents live in poverty. The city covers 18.01 square miles of land, so density reaches 11,749.9 people per square mile. Mean commute is 35.6 minutes.

The city rises from the Hudson River up seven hills, and its downtown is Getty Square. It has been a city since 1872 and that it stayed outside New York City when the 1898 consolidation was voted on. Check recent sales on your own block, since a citywide median hides neighborhood differences.

What should I check before selling a Yonkers house with tax due?

Start with the online parcel record, then confirm the exact figure with the Tax Office. Because installments carry no grace period, the date matters.

  • List which of the July, October and January installments are paid, and whether the April county bill is paid.
  • Ask for the interest through the planned closing date at 15 percent a year.
  • Check the exemption renewal date on October 15.
  • Find out whether a Board of Assessment Review complaint or a small claims case is pending.

A cash buyer does not need the taxes cleared first. The title company pays the open balances out of your proceeds at closing, and the Yonkers Tax Office can supply the payoff.

Frequently asked questions

When is the next Yonkers property tax installment due?

The third city and school installment is due Wednesday, January 6, 2027. The next county bill is usually adopted in March and due 30 days later, with the 2026 date having been April 14.

How much is the late interest on Yonkers property tax?

It is 15 percent a year, simple interest, calculated daily from the confirmation date. There is no grace period, and the city says the interest cannot be waived for any reason.

When can I file a Yonkers assessment complaint?

From November 1 to November 15 with the Board of Assessment Review. Supporting documents and personal hearing requests are due by December 15, and hearings begin on the last Monday in January.

Where do I pay Yonkers taxes in person?

At the Cashier's Office on the first floor of City Hall, 40 South Broadway, Room 108. You can also mail a check to the same address or pay online by credit card or electronic check.

How can a title company get Yonkers tax information?

Title companies can use the online property portal and the municipal tax payment site for free. A $5 fee per property per year applies if the Tax Department does the research, with two to three weeks of lead time.
